method_note: Scale established per plate. Where a graduated scale bar exists its decimetre/metre graduations were located and px/m computed. Where only the textual scale ('Échelle de 0.05 c.m pour mètre') exists, px/m was recovered from printed dimension callouts on the same plate (tick-to-tick pixel span / printed metres). Cross-check: the scanned sheets reproduce at a constant ~56.9 px per cm of paper for portrait plates (1920x~2570) and ~42.7 px/cm for landscape plates (1920x~1430); every scale bar measured on this group agreed with that within 2%. Printed callouts are always preferred over pixel measurement.

plates.notes: A two-light entresol window flanked by caryatid consoles. Contrast with plate 57 (No 120 Sébastopol) whose entresol window is a single squat opening of h/w 1.23 — entresol windows in this corpus are not one shape.
